title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: Gospel promise — seed of woman; common remedy ≠ imputation
pass_a_gloss: Next you claim the same from the Gospel promise at v. 15 about the woman's seed—Christ who will crush the serpent's head as the race's avenger. From a shared penalty you infer a shared sin; likewise from a shared Remedy to wipe that sin away you infer the sin was everyone's. Placeus grants a first shared sin, but located in the corruption set in all, not in charging Adam's actual deed; and made shared by fleshly generation, not by God's charging it.
pass_b_english: You add that the same is demonstrated from the promise of the Gospel inserted there in verse 15 concerning the seed of the woman, Christ namely the avenger of the human race, who will crush the serpent's head. Just as from a common penalty it is inferred that the sin was common, so from a common Remedy for blotting out that sin it follows that that sin was common to all. But I confess a first common sin, yet seated not in the imputation of Adam's actual sin, but in corruption implanted in all; and made common not by divine imputation, but by carnal generation.
source_text: Addis, idem demonstrari ex promissione Evangelii illic inserta vers. 15. de semine mulieris, Christo scilicet vindice generis humani, contrituro caput serpentis. Quemadmodum ex poena communi infertur peccatum fuisse commune, sic ex Remedio communi ad delendum illud peccatum, sequitur illud peccatum fuisse omnibus commune. At primum commune fateor peccatum, sed situm, non in imputatione peccati actualis Adami, sed in corruptione omnibus insita; & commune factum, non imputatione divina, sed generatione carnali.
